From Middle English saien, sain, san, secgan, segen, seien, sein, seiȝen, sugen, sægen, ziggen, from Old English seċġan, secgean, secggan, secggean, seggan, sæċġan (“to say, speak”), from Proto-West Germanic *saggjan, from Proto-Germanic *sagjaną (“to say”), from Proto-Indo-European

s.d: the chance to speak
x: let him have his say

s.d: (uncountable) A chance to speak; the right or power to influence or make a decision.
x: The local government did not have much say in the matter.
Above all, however, we would like to think that there is more to be decided, after the engines and after the humans have had their says.

s.d: (uncountable) A type of fine cloth similar to serge.
x: Per.[igot] VVell decked in a frocke of gray, / Will.[y] hey ho, gray is greet, / Per. And in a kirtle of greene ſaye, / Will. the greene is for maydens meete.
All in a kirtle of diſcolourd ſay / He clothed was […]

s.d: Trial by sample; assay; specimen.
x: If those principal works of God […] be but certain tastes and says, as if were, of that final benefit.
Thy tongue some say of breeding breathes.

s.d: Tried quality; temper; proof.
x: He found a sword of better say.

s.d: Essay; trial; attempt.
x: This fellow, Captaine, Will come, in time, to be a great distiller, And giue a say[…]at the philosophers stone.

s.d: (Scotland) A strainer for milk.
express in words
x: He said that he wanted to marry her
tell me what is bothering you

s.d: report or maintain
x: He alleged that he was the victim of a crime
He said it was too late to intervene in the war

s.d: express a supposition
x: Let us say that he did not tell the truth
Let's say you had a lot of money — what would you do?

s.d: have or contain a certain wording or form
x: The passage reads as follows
What does the law say?

s.d: give instructions to or direct somebody to do something with authority
x: I said to him to go home
She ordered him to do the shopping

s.d: speak, pronounce, or utter in a certain way
x: She pronounces French words in a funny way
I cannot say ‘zip wire’

s.d: communicate or express nonverbally
x: What does this painting say?
Did his face say anything about how he felt?

s.d: utter aloud
x: She said ‘Hello’ to everyone in the office

s.d: state as one's opinion or judgement; declare
x: I say let's forget this whole business

s.d: recite or repeat a fixed text
x: Say grace
She said her ‘Hail Mary’

s.d: indicate
x: The clock says noon

s.d: To pronounce.
x: Please say your name slowly and clearly.

s.d: To recite.
x: Martha, will you say the Pledge of Allegiance?

s.d: To tell, either verbally or in writing.
x: He said he would be here tomorrow.
The note I think he said she wrote is nowhere to be found.

s.d: To indicate in a written form.
x: The sign says it’s 50 kilometres to Paris.
What time does it say on the clock?

s.d: To have a common expression; used in singular passive voice or plural active voice to indicate a rumor or well-known fact.
x: They say "when in Rome, do as the Romans do", which means "behave as those around you do."
They say that Hope is happiness; But genuine Love must prize the past.

s.d: (informal) Suppose, assume; used to mark an example, supposition or hypothesis.
x: A holiday somewhere warm – Florida, say – would be nice.
Say he refuses. What do we do then?

s.d: To speak; to express an opinion; to make answer; to reply.
x: You have said; but whether wisely or no, let the forest judge
To this argument we shall soon have said; for what concerns it us to hear a husband divulge his household privacies?

s.d: (informal) To bet as a wager on an outcome; by extension, used to express belief in an outcome by the speaker.
x: 'My fifty pounds says three months after the invasion there'll be a free press in Iraq, and unmonitored internet access too.'

s.d: To try; to assay.
x: I, that had sayed on one of his customers sutes.

s.d: For example; let us assume.
x: Pick a color you think they'd like, say, peach.
He was driving pretty fast, say, fifty miles per hour.

s.d: (US, colloquial) Used to gain someone's attention before making an inquiry or suggestion
x: Say, what did you think about the movie?

s.d: say good-bye or bid farewell

say-so.e: From say + so. Compare says who.

s.d: one chap's arbitrary assertion
an authoritative declaration
the power or right to give orders or make decisions
x: he has the authority to issue warrants
deputies are given authorization to make arrests

s.d: (informal) Authority, as backing some statement, injunction, or command.
x: I wouldn't buy anything that expensive just on the say-so of a saleman.
You are not to go into that room without my say-so.

s.d: Israel's elite secret commando unit responsible for counterterrorist and top secret intelligence gathering and hostage rescue missions

s.d: A proverb or maxim.

sayonara.e: Borrowed from Japanese さようなら (sayōnara, “farewell”, literally “if that's the way it is”) or its shorter, less traditional form さよなら (sayonara).

s.d: a farewell remark
x: they said their good-byes

s.d: An utterance of sayonara, the wishing of farewell to someone.
x: After a simply marvelous, entertaining two and a half hour meal, they reclaimed their shoes and ceremoniously bid their sayonaras to the Japanese girls.

s.d: (humorous, informal) Goodbye, adios, adieu.
x: Sonic: Sayonara! Shadow the Hedgehog!
